category_groups.label: Schools
category_groups.one_liner: Pays for K-12 public schools and the local community college.
category_groups.explanation: This is the single biggest slice of your tax bill -- typically over half. It covers your local school district (teachers, buildings, buses), a regional education service district that supports smaller schools, and Southwestern Oregon Community College. Some of this may include voter-approved bonds for specific building projects.

category_groups.label: Fire & Emergency
category_groups.one_liner: Funds your local fire department -- staff, trucks, and equipment.
category_groups.explanation: Curry County has over a dozen separate fire districts, each covering a different area. You're only taxed by the one that covers your property. This pays for firefighters (often volunteer), fire trucks, and emergency response equipment.

category_groups.label: County Government
category_groups.one_liner: Runs core county services: the Sheriff's Office, courts, roads, and administration.
category_groups.explanation: This is the slice that funds Curry County's own government -- things like the Sheriff's Office and jail, the District Attorney, road maintenance, and the offices that run elections and process your property records. It's a smaller share than most people expect: only about 7 cents of every property tax dollar.

category_groups.label: City Government
category_groups.one_liner: Funds your city government, if you live inside city limits.
category_groups.explanation: Only applies if your property is inside Port Orford, Gold Beach, or Brookings. It pays for city services like police (where the city has its own department), parks, and city administration. Properties outside city limits don't pay this.

category_groups.label: Health District
category_groups.one_liner: Supports local public health services and facilities.
category_groups.explanation: Curry County has a health district that funds public health programs and, in part, healthcare facility costs. This includes a voter-approved bond for specific health facility projects.

category_groups.label: Library
category_groups.explanation: Curry County has several library districts covering different communities. Yours pays for library staff, books, programs, and building upkeep for whichever library district covers your property.

category_groups.label: Roads
category_groups.one_liner: A small local levy for road maintenance in specific areas.
category_groups.explanation: Most road funding in Curry County comes from state gas tax revenue, not property tax -- so this line is usually small or zero. It only applies to a few specific road districts.

category_groups.label: Other Local Districts
category_groups.one_liner: Smaller local districts: ports, cemeteries, water, sewer, and downtown revitalization projects.
category_groups.explanation: This bucket groups several smaller special districts that only apply in specific areas: port districts (harbor and marina upkeep), cemetery districts, water and sanitary (sewer) districts, and urban renewal districts (which fund downtown improvement projects in Brookings and Gold Beach). Most properties are only in one or two of these, not all.

assessed_value.short_definition: The dollar figure the county uses to calculate your tax bill -- usually lower than what your home would actually sell for.
assessed_value.longer_note: Oregon law limits how fast assessed value can grow each year, so in many cases it's well below market value, especially for homes that have been owned a long time.

real_market_value.short_definition: The county's estimate of what your property would sell for today.
real_market_value.longer_note: This is different from assessed value (see above) and is not what your tax bill is based on.

tax_rate.short_definition: How much you pay per $1,000 of assessed value.
tax_rate.longer_note: Example: a rate of $2.50 means you pay $2.50 for every $1,000 of your property's assessed value. A $300,000 assessed home at that rate pays $750/year for that one district.

levy.short_definition: A tax a district is authorized to collect.
levy.longer_note: Districts don't set their own rate freely -- their levy is approved either permanently (voted in once, applies every year) or as a local option (voted in for a limited number of years).

permanent_rate.short_definition: A tax rate that was voted in once and continues every year without needing renewal.
permanent_rate.longer_note: Most of the county, school, and fire district base rates are permanent rates.

local_option_levy.short_definition: An additional tax rate voters approved for a limited number of years, on top of the permanent rate.
local_option_levy.longer_note: These expire and have to be renewed by voters, unlike permanent rates.

bond.short_definition: A tax specifically for paying back money borrowed for a big one-time project, like a new school or hospital building.
bond.longer_note: Bonds are temporary -- they end once the borrowed money is paid off, usually after 15-20 years. They're listed separately from a district's regular operating rate.

urban_renewal.short_definition: A program where a city sets aside a slice of tax growth in a specific district to fund improvement projects there (like downtown revitalization).
urban_renewal.longer_note: It doesn't directly add to your tax rate the way other districts do -- instead it redirects some of the growth in property value within the renewal area toward local improvement projects, which can mean other districts collect slightly less from that specific area.

code_area.short_definition: A small zone where every property is taxed by the exact same combination of districts.
code_area.longer_note: Curry County has about 45 of these. Two neighbors can be in different code areas -- and pay different total rates -- if one is covered by a different fire or water district.

taxing_district.short_definition: Any local government or agency allowed to collect property tax, like a school district, fire district, or library district.
taxing_district.longer_note: Curry County has around 48 separate taxing districts. Most properties fall within somewhere between 6 and 12 of them at once.

compression_m5.short_definition: A constitutional cap that can reduce your tax bill if the combined rate for schools or general government gets too high.
compression_m5.longer_note: This is a technical Oregon-specific safeguard; most residents won't need this explained beyond 'there's a legal ceiling on how high your combined rate can go.'

headline_facts.stat: For every $1 you pay in property tax, about 7 cents goes to Curry County government -- the rest goes to schools, fire districts, and other local services.
Schools take the biggest share of your tax bill -- about 56 cents of every dollar.
If you live inside Port Orford, Gold Beach, or Brookings, city government adds about another 15 cents of every dollar. Outside city limits, that share goes to zero.

dollar_story_formula.description: Guidance for turning a district's rate into a plain dollar figure for a hypothetical home. Don't hardcode a single example value -- compute this live from whatever assessed value the user enters (or a sensible default like $300,000, the app's home page could default to Curry County's approximate median).
dollar_story_formula.example_for_copy_only: A $300,000 assessed home at a rate of $0.6609 per $1,000 pays about $198/year to that one district. (300000/1000)*0.6609 = 198.27

headline_stats.opening_section_copy: Curious where your property tax dollars actually go? Curry County collects tax on behalf of about 48 different local agencies -- your county government is just one of them, and usually the smallest slice. Enter your home's assessed value below to see your own estimated breakdown, or explore the countywide averages.
headline_stats.caveat_copy: This is an estimate based on published FY2025-26 tax rates and your area's typical mix of districts. Your actual bill may vary slightly and is set by the Curry County Assessor's Office -- see your tax statement or contact the Assessor for the exact figure.
